scope: Independent external fault-controller, observer placement, protocol/filesystem injection and complete receipt review; Linux short-stage only
reviewer: root (not author of the fault/observer implementation)

findings.finding: A historical distinct backend PID is insufficient to prove the retry used a replacement physical session.
findings.resolution: 411f99d binds a new INSERT after the recorded protocol sequence barrier to its actual backend PID.

findings.finding: An empty provider inventory or truncated native-counter vector could pass a universal zero check.
findings.resolution: 411f99d requires the exact provider set and six counters per module.

findings.finding: An outer cleanup failure or interruption could publish a passed partial prefix.
findings.resolution: 0f98145635658adaedf06176bd86ec373d7eca00 writes final status once after exact selected IDs, all case statuses and completed outer lifecycle.
findings.applicability: Final001 unchanged observations contain all required40 cases, each outer process exited0 and both PostgreSQL stop logs confirm server stopped. This source-only receipt finalization fix does not relabel executed artifacts or rerun unrelated fault observations.

verdict: Short fault matrix reviewed; no open finding in this scope. Full B22 acceptance remains false.
limitations: Observed consumer changes only Main accessibility and selects a wrapper whose application task/thread are joined before final GC; the application body and native assets are unchanged.
ProcessExit before entrypoint release was an observer lifetime artifact, not demonstrated B21 leakage.
Intentional SIGKILL is not graceful resource retirement or a power-loss guarantee.
Scoped libc WAL ENOSPC is injected I/O failure, not physical whole-disk exhaustion.
Runtime GCHandle controls are separate process-level observations; neither procfs nor native owner counters count every managed root.
